api:
<Heatmap> shows how values are spread over two dimensions, usually how many samples fell into each time × value bucket. It's a port of Grafana's Heatmap panel; see Coming from Grafana.

Where the cells come from

You havePassCells
raw samples, such as one row per requestx, y and calculatethe samples are counted into buckets
one row per cell, already countedx, y and value (plus x_end / y_end if cells have different sizes)one cell per row, starting at x / y
bucket fields, such as a Prometheus histograma Frame: x first, then one field per bucket, named by its boundone row of cells per field

Calculation follows Grafana's "Calculate from data":

Calculation { x_buckets: Buckets::Size(60_000.), y_buckets: Buckets::Count(20), y_scale: BucketScale::Linear }
FieldValues
x_buckets / y_bucketsBuckets::Auto (about 20 columns and 10 rows), Buckets::Count(n) (about n, rounded to a tidy size), Buckets::Size(s) (exactly s wide)
y_scaleBucketScale::Linear, Log2 or Log10. With a log scale, Buckets::Size(n) splits each power into n buckets

With a time x axis, column sizes are rounded to whole seconds, minutes, hours and so on.

Bucket fields. By default each field becomes one evenly spaced row, labelled with the field name:

  • BucketLayout::Le: names are upper bounds, as Prometheus le buckets are; the label sits on the row's top edge.
  • Ge: names are lower bounds.
  • Auto: labels sit in the middle of each row.

Set bucket_scale to place the rows by the numbers in their names instead, on that scale. +Inf is drawn as one more bucket.

Colour

HeatmapColorCells are coloured
HeatmapColor::scheme(HeatmapScheme::…)along one of Grafana's 38 colour schemes
HeatmapColor::theme(Scheme::…)along a scheme from your theme
HeatmapColor::opacity(color)in one colour, more opaque for higher values
MethodEffectDefault
.steps(n)how many distinct colours, 2–12864
.reverse(bool)flips a schemefalse
.exponent(e)opacity mode: 0.1–2.0; below 1 makes low values stand out morelinear

The scheme colours are exactly Grafana's (d3-scale-chromatic). As in Grafana, the diverging and cyclical schemes are flipped. Single-hue schemes (Blues, Oranges, …) are flipped in dark mode, so high values are bright on a dark background. Multi-hue schemes (Viridis, Magma, Turbo, …) are flipped in light mode.

color_min / color_max fix the ends of the colour range. Values beyond them use the end colours.

Cells

  • cell_gap leaves space between cells; it's ignored on cells too small to fit it.
  • show_value: Auto writes the value in cells wide enough for it, Always writes it everywhere, Never writes none.
  • cell_format or cell_decimals set the value text, used in cells, the tooltip and the legend.
  • hide_le hides cells at or below a value; the default 1e-9 hides empty buckets. Pass f64::NEG_INFINITY to show every cell. hide_ge hides cells at or above a value.
  • exemplars draws individual points over the cells, such as single slow requests.

Axes and time

Both axes take an AxisConfig. Three methods matter most here:

MethodEffect
AxisConfig::new().time()values are milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Ticks fall on round times and read HH:mm:ss, HH:mm, MM/DD HH:mm, MM/DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY depending on the span. Shown in UTC
.utc_offset(minutes)shows times in another time zone, such as 120 for UTC+2
.reverse(true)turns the axis upside down

The x axis spans exactly the first to the last bucket.

Zooming and selection

Drag across the cells to zoom in, and double-click to zoom back out.

SelectionModeDragging zooms
Xthe x axis
Ythe y axis
XYboth, using the box you draw

on_select receives the range too: a SelectedRange { x: (from, to), y: Option<(from, to)> }. Use it to move your app's time range to the selection.

examples.title: Latency over time
examples.description: Raw request samples, counted into 4-minute by 20 ms buckets.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn latency() {
    let data = use_signal(requests());
    rsx! {
        <Heatmap data={data} x={|r: &Request| r.time} y={|r| r.latency} calculate={calc()} x_axis={time()} y_axis={AxisConfig::new().label("ms")} class="h-72" />
    }
}

examples.title: Log buckets
examples.code:
#[component]
fn log_buckets() {
    let data = use_signal(requests());
    rsx! {
        <Heatmap
            data={data}
            x={|r: &Request| r.time}
            y={|r| r.latency}
            calculate={Calculation { x_buckets: Buckets::Count(30), y_buckets: Buckets::Size(4.), y_scale: BucketScale::Log2 }}
            color={HeatmapColor::scheme(HeatmapScheme::Viridis)}
            x_axis={time()}
            class="h-72"
        />
    }
}

examples.title: Histogram buckets
examples.description: Prometheus-style bucket fields (le), one row per bucket.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn prometheus() {
    let data = use_signal(histogram());
    rsx! {
        <Heatmap data={data} bucket_layout={BucketLayout::Le} color={HeatmapColor::scheme(HeatmapScheme::Spectral)} x_axis={time()} class="h-72" />
    }
}

examples.title: Cells with values
examples.description: One row per cell, values shown in every cell, gaps and rounded corners.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn week() {
    let data = use_signal(deploys());
    rsx! {
        <Heatmap
            data={data}
            x={|s: &Slot| s.hour}
            y={|s| s.day}
            value={|s| s.deploys}
            show_value={VisibilityMode::Always}
            hide_le={f64::NEG_INFINITY}
            cell_gap={3.}
            cell_radius={4.}
            color={HeatmapColor::scheme(HeatmapScheme::Greens)}
            y_axis={AxisConfig::new().reverse(true).format(|day| DAYS.get(day as usize).copied().unwrap_or("").into())}
            x_axis={AxisConfig::new().format(|hour| format!("{hour:02}:00").into())}
            class="h-72"
        />
    }
}

examples.title: Exemplars
examples.description: Individual samples marked over the buckets.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn exemplars() {
    let data = use_signal(requests());
    let marks: Vec<(f64, f64)> = (0..6)
        .map(|step| {
            (
                T0 + f64::from(step) * 20. * MINUTE + 5. * MINUTE,
                380. - f64::from(step) * 30.,
            )
        })
        .collect();
    rsx! {
        <Heatmap data={data} x={|r: &Request| r.time} y={|r| r.latency} calculate={calc()} exemplars={marks} x_axis={time()} class="h-72" />
    }
}

examples.title: Box zoom
examples.description: Drag to zoom into both axes; on_select reports the range.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn zoom() {
    let data = use_signal(requests());
    let picked = use_signal(SharedString::Borrowed(
        "Drag a box over the cells. Double-click to zoom out.",
    ));
    rsx! {
        <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 h-72">
            <div class="text-xs">{picked.get()}</div>
            <Heatmap
                data={data}
                x={|r: &Request| r.time}
                y={|r| r.latency}
                calculate={calc()}
                selection={SelectionMode::XY}
                on_select={move |range: SelectedRange, _: &mut Window, _: &mut App| {
                    let (low, high) = range.y.unwrap_or_default();
                    picked.set(SharedString::from(format!("Selected {low:.0}–{high:.0} ms")));
                }}
                x_axis={time()}
                class="flex-1"
            />
        </div>
    }
}

examples.title: Live data
examples.description: A signal as data: the heatmap redraws when it changes.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn live() {
    let data = use_signal(requests());
    rsx! {
        <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 h-72">
            <div id="slower" class="cursor-pointer text-sm underline" onClick={move || data.update(|rows| rows.iter_mut().for_each(|r| r.latency *= 1.15))}>
                "Make it 15% slower"
            </div>
            <Heatmap data={data} x={|r: &Request| r.time} y={|r| r.latency} calculate={calc()} x_axis={time()} class="flex-1" />
        </div>
    }
}
